# Causal result `of`

When an adnominal `of` phrase names the inanimate producer of a result, label that complement `p.Force` in the scene. In `the rewards of this program`, the program produces the rewards, so `of this program` is `p.Force, p.Force`; do not default to `p.Gestalt, p.Gestalt` merely because `of` connects two nouns.

Use the noun and context to establish causation. Ordinary association and possession retain their supported labels: `Stuart's strategies` is `p.Gestalt, p.Gestalt`; `our business` is `p.OrgMember, p.Possessor`. An animate maker in `your contributions` is `p.Agent, p.Gestalt`. Other `of` relations remain distinct: `Each of you` is `p.QuantityItem, p.Whole`, and `proud of your contributions` is `p.Stimulus, p.Topic`. A causal scene role does not always imply a Force lexical function: `the devastation of the fire on the town` is `p.Force, p.Gestalt`.
